quests.hint: The list of topics to be discussed at a meeting.
quests.explanation: An agenda lists the topics of a meeting. We 'set', 'send' or 'go through' an agenda. 'Hidden agenda' is a different idiom about secret motives.
quests.textToSpeak: Let's go through the ___ first so we all know what we're covering today.
quests.correctAnswer: Let's go through the agenda first so we all know what we're covering today.
quests.contextClue: Knowing what will be covered points to a list.

quests.hint: The official written record of what was said and decided at a meeting.
quests.explanation: The formal record of a meeting is called the minutes, and it is always plural. Casual notes are less formal.
quests.textToSpeak: Could someone write up the ___ of today's meeting? They need to go to the whole board.
quests.correctAnswer: Could someone write up the minutes of today's meeting? They need to go to the whole board.
quests.contextClue: A record sent to the board needs to be formal.

quests.hint: Moved to a later date.
quests.explanation: 'Postponed until' + a later time means delayed on purpose. It differs from 'cancelled', which means it won't happen at all.
quests.textToSpeak: The meeting has been ___ until next week because the manager is ill.
quests.correctAnswer: The meeting has been postponed until next week because the manager is ill.
quests.contextClue: 'Until next week' shows a new, later date.

quests.hint: The plan showing when things should be done.
quests.explanation: 'Behind schedule' means later than planned. The related phrases are 'ahead of schedule' and 'on schedule'.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm swamped this week. I have three reports due, and I'm already behind ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm swamped this week. I have three reports due, and I'm already behind schedule.
quests.contextClue: Three reports due and being swamped suggest running late.

quests.hint: Needing attention right away.
quests.explanation: 'Urgent' means needing immediate action, while 'important' means significant but not always immediate. 'Fairly urgent' is a polite way of pressing.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you get back to me by the end of the day? It's fairly ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Could you get back to me by the end of the day? It's fairly urgent.
quests.contextClue: A same-day deadline shows time pressure.

quests.hint: The amount of work you have to do.
quests.explanation: 'Workload' is the amount of work assigned to a person. Common pairs: 'heavy workload' and 'manageable workload'.
quests.textToSpeak: My ___ has doubled since two colleagues left, and I can't keep up.
quests.correctAnswer: My workload has doubled since two colleagues left, and I can't keep up.
quests.contextClue: Doubling and 'can't keep up' describe too much assigned work.

quests.hint: Joined to a message so you can open it.
quests.explanation: 'Please find the report attached' is a standard email phrase. 'Attached' also works as an adjective: 'the attached file'.
quests.textToSpeak: Please find the report ___ to this email.
quests.correctAnswer: Please find the report attached to this email.
quests.contextClue: A report sent with an email is joined to it.

quests.hint: The place where many people work at desks.
quests.explanation: 'Out of the office' is the standard phrase for being away from work. It is also used in automatic email replies.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry for the late reply. I've been out of the ___ all week.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry for the late reply. I've been out of the office all week.
quests.contextClue: A late reply is explained by being away from work.

quests.hint: A message that helps you remember something.
quests.explanation: 'Just a quick reminder that...' is a friendly way to start an email. The noun comes from the verb 'remind'.
quests.textToSpeak: Just a quick ___ that the form is due on Friday.
quests.correctAnswer: Just a quick reminder that the form is due on Friday.
quests.contextClue: Restating the Friday date works as a prompt.

quests.hint: A short summary of the main points.
quests.explanation: An overview gives the big picture before the details. In presentations, 'a brief overview' or 'a quick overview' is common.
quests.textToSpeak: I'll start with a brief ___ of the project and then look at the results.
quests.correctAnswer: I'll start with a brief overview of the project and then look at the results.
quests.contextClue: 'Brief' and 'start with' set an opening summary.

quests.hint: What the audience asks at the end of a talk.
quests.explanation: At the end of a presentation, speakers say 'I'm happy to take questions'. 'Take questions' means answer them.
quests.textToSpeak: That's all from me. Thank you for listening, and I'm happy to take any ___.
quests.correctAnswer: That's all from me. Thank you for listening, and I'm happy to take any questions.
quests.contextClue: The end of a talk invites the audience to ask.

quests.hint: One page of a presentation shown on a screen.
quests.explanation: In presentations we say 'on the next slide' or 'on this slide'. The whole set is a slide deck or a slideshow.
quests.textToSpeak: On the next ___ you'll see the results broken down by region.
quests.correctAnswer: On the next slide you'll see the results broken down by region.
quests.contextClue: A presentation shows one visual page at a time.

quests.hint: Responsible for looking after something.
quests.explanation: 'In charge of' means responsible for: 'in charge of the team'. 'Take charge' means take control.
quests.textToSpeak: Who is in ___ of the budget for this project?
quests.correctAnswer: Who is in charge of the budget for this project?
quests.contextClue: The question asks who has responsibility for money.

quests.hint: Movement forward toward a goal.
quests.explanation: Progress is uncountable: 'good progress', 'make progress'. We don't say 'a progress' or 'progresses' in this meaning.
quests.textToSpeak: Our team has made good ___ this month, and we're nearly finished.
quests.correctAnswer: Our team has made good progress this month, and we're nearly finished.
quests.contextClue: 'Nearly finished' shows the work moved forward.

quests.hint: Gave help, effort or ideas toward a shared goal.
quests.explanation: 'Contribute to' means give your part to a shared result: 'contribute to the project'. Note the preposition 'to'.
quests.textToSpeak: Thanks to everyone who ___ to the project; it wouldn't have worked without you.
quests.correctAnswer: Thanks to everyone who contributed to the project; it wouldn't have worked without you.
quests.contextClue: A thank-you shows that people gave their part.

quests.hint: What you have learned by doing jobs over the years.
quests.explanation: In interviews, 'work experience' means jobs you have done. In this meaning it is uncountable: 'a lot of experience', not 'experiences'.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you tell me a little about your previous work ___?
quests.correctAnswer: Could you tell me a little about your previous work experience?
quests.contextClue: An interviewer asks about earlier jobs.

quests.hint: A document you send with a CV to introduce yourself.
quests.explanation: A cover letter accompanies a CV or résumé. 'CV' is common in British English, and Americans often say 'résumé'.
quests.textToSpeak: I've attached my CV and a cover ___ explaining why I want the role.
quests.correctAnswer: I've attached my CV and a cover letter explaining why I want the role.
quests.contextClue: Explaining motivation is done in a document that goes with a CV.

quests.hint: Things you do especially well.
quests.explanation: In interviews, 'strengths and weaknesses' are qualities you are good or bad at. The plural is common: 'my greatest strengths'.
quests.textToSpeak: What would you say are your greatest ___? Are you better at planning or at teamwork?
quests.correctAnswer: What would you say are your greatest strengths? Are you better at planning or at teamwork?
quests.contextClue: The follow-up mentions things the candidate does well.

quests.hint: Easy to talk to.
quests.explanation: 'Approachable' describes someone friendly and easy to talk to. Its opposite is 'unapproachable'.
quests.textToSpeak: Our new manager is very ___; you can talk to her about anything.
quests.correctAnswer: Our new manager is very approachable; you can talk to her about anything.
quests.contextClue: 'Talk to her about anything' shows openness.

quests.hint: The small word that links 'report' with your boss's title.
quests.explanation: 'Report to' + person means that person is your manager: 'I report to Sara'.
quests.textToSpeak: Officially I report ___ the head of finance, but I work with the sales team every day.
quests.correctAnswer: Officially I report to the head of finance, but I work with the sales team every day.
quests.contextClue: The speaker's line manager is named by title.

quests.hint: Take someone's place for a short time.
quests.explanation: 'Fill in for' someone means do their job while they are away. 'Fill in' also means complete a form.
quests.textToSpeak: Could you ___ in for me on Friday? I have to go to a family event.
quests.correctAnswer: Could you fill in for me on Friday? I have to go to a family event.
quests.contextClue: Missing work for an event needs a replacement.

quests.hint: A piece of structured writing on a subject, common in school.
quests.explanation: An essay is a structured piece of writing. We 'write' or 'hand in' an essay. It differs from a report or an article.
quests.textToSpeak: For my literature class, I have to write a two-thousand-word ___ on a novel of my choice.
quests.correctAnswer: For my literature class, I have to write a two-thousand-word essay on a novel of my choice.
quests.contextClue: A literature class and a word count describe a school text.

quests.hint: The document that lists what a course will cover.
quests.explanation: A syllabus outlines the topics and readings of a course. The plural is 'syllabuses' or 'syllabi'.
quests.textToSpeak: Check the ___ to see which chapters we need to read before the exam.
quests.correctAnswer: Check the syllabus to see which chapters we need to read before the exam.
quests.contextClue: The document tells students which chapters to read.

quests.hint: More time added to a limit.
quests.explanation: An extension is extra time to finish something. We 'ask for', 'get' or 'give' an extension.
quests.textToSpeak: Because I was ill, my lecturer gave me an ___ on the deadline.
quests.correctAnswer: Because I was ill, my lecturer gave me an extension on the deadline.
quests.contextClue: Illness explains why extra time was granted.

quests.hint: Happens at the same time as something else, causing a problem.
quests.explanation: 'Clash with' is used when two events happen at the same time: 'The concert clashes with my exam.' American English often prefers 'conflict'.
quests.textToSpeak: Sorry, I can't join at ten. It ___ with another meeting.
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, I can't join at ten. It clashes with another meeting.
quests.contextClue: Being unable to join explains a scheduling problem.

quests.hint: Not closed; with nothing planned.
quests.explanation: 'Wide open' means completely free or without restrictions: 'my afternoon is wide open'. It is a casual way to say you have no commitments.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm booked solid this morning, but my afternoon is wide ___.
quests.correctAnswer: I'm booked solid this morning, but my afternoon is wide open.
quests.contextClue: A booked morning contrasts with a free afternoon.

quests.hint: Free and able to do something at a given time.
quests.explanation: 'Available' is common in work settings: 'Are you available on Monday?' It is slightly more formal than 'free'.
quests.textToSpeak: Are you ___ for a quick call at three?
quests.correctAnswer: Are you available for a quick call at three?
quests.contextClue: A specific time is proposed and the person is asked whether they are free then.

quests.hint: Find a solution to a problem or disagreement.
quests.explanation: 'Resolve' is common for disagreements and misunderstandings, while 'solve' fits problems with a clear answer.
quests.textToSpeak: There's been a misunderstanding about the order, and we need to ___ it before the client finds out.
quests.correctAnswer: There's been a misunderstanding about the order, and we need to resolve it before the client finds out.
quests.contextClue: A misunderstanding needs to be settled.

quests.hint: Bring goods or results as promised.
quests.explanation: 'Fail to deliver' means not provide what was promised. 'Deliver on time' is common in business.
quests.textToSpeak: Our supplier failed to ___ on time, so we had to delay the launch.
quests.correctAnswer: Our supplier failed to deliver on time, so we had to delay the launch.
quests.contextClue: A late supply caused the delay.

quests.hint: A job that nobody is doing yet.
quests.explanation: A vacancy is an unfilled job. We say 'a job vacancy' or 'fill a vacancy'. In hotels it also means a free room.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a ___ in our department, and they're advertising it online.
quests.correctAnswer: There's a vacancy in our department, and they're advertising it online.
quests.contextClue: Advertising online suggests a role that needs someone.
